title: Apollo 10 - CSM Charlie Brown, LM Snoopy
_comment: Apollo 10, the first lunar landing's dress rehearsal: the LM flew down to 8 nmi over the first landing's site, staged in orbit and flew the landing mission's rendezvous back to the CSM, without landing. Sources: the Apollo 10 Mission Report (MSC-00126), the Apollo/Saturn V Postflight Trajectory for AS-505 (Boeing D5-15560-5), the S-IVB-505N flight evaluation report, the spacecraft operational trajectory for Apollo 10, revision 1, volume I (MSC Internal Note 69-FM-96), the final flight plan and the Apollo Flight Journal's transcript. Distances in km, times in GET seconds or hhh:mm:ss (GET counts from range zero, 16:49:00 UTC on 18 May 1969).

call_signs._comment: The call signs CAPCOM used for the flight and, once they flew apart, for its vehicles (Apollo Flight Journal) [published]; CAPCOM's own calls on the timeline say Snoop and 10 where he did

start_calls.launch: T minus 20 seconds and counting. Guidance internal.
start_calls.translunar_coast: {mission}, Houston. Good trajectory. Your evasive maneuver PAD is coming up.
start_calls.lunar_orbit: {mission}, Houston. You're in a 61 by 59-mile orbit with {lm} docked. GO for undocking comes on the twelfth rev.
start_calls.lunar_descent: {lm}, Houston. You're on the descent orbit, down to 8 miles over site 2 in twenty minutes. The phasing PAD comes before the low pass.
start_calls.tei: {csm}, Houston. {lm}'s ascent stage is gone, and your TEI PAD is on its way up.
start_calls.transearth_coast: Houston: TEI was good. Your midcourse PADs will come up to trim the entry corridor.
start_calls.entry: Houston: entry interface in about twenty minutes. P61, CM/SM SEP when P62 asks, ELS LOGIC and AUTO.
start_calls._comment: CAPCOM's word as each start phase begins, the simulator's own [adapted]

vehicles._comment: Apollo 10's vehicles where they differ from data/spacecraft.json's, Apollo 11's

mass._source: The mission report's mass properties (MSC-00126, Table A.4-I: the CSM 63,560 lb before transposition and docking, the CM 12,138 lb after CM/SM separation; the LM 31,166 lb at its separation, 30,283 lb after the phasing burn, its ascent stage 8,273 lb after staging) and propellant loads (sections 7.11 and 8.13: the SPS's 40,806 lb, the SM RCS's 1,340.9 lb, the CM RCS's 244.5 lb; the DPS's 18,218.7 lb, of which DOI and the phasing burn used 765 lb; the APS's 2,631 lb, half a load; the LM RCS's 634 lb) [published]; the vehicle at the S-IVB's second ignition, 292,191 lb (the S-IVB-505N flight evaluation report, Table 8-1) [published]. From them [derived]: the CM dry of its RCS's propellant, the SM dry of its own and the SPS's; the descent stage dry, the LM after phasing less the ascent stage after staging and the DPS's propellant left; the ascent stage dry, with the crew and their equipment, the LM at its separation less the rest [simplified: the LM carries its crew from TLI, 431 lb more than its 30,735 lb at launch]; the S-IVB dry with the Instrument Unit, the adapter and the residuals, the vehicle at ignition less the CSM, the LM and the propellant

sps._source: The SPS's load, 40,806 lb (MSC-00126, section 7.11.1) [published]; its engine Apollo 11's

sm_rcs._source: The SM RCS's load, 1,340.9 lb in four quads (MSC-00126, section 7.11.2) [published]

cm_rcs._source: The CM RCS's load, 244.5 lb in two systems (MSC-00126, section 7.11.2) [published]

dps._source: The DPS's load, 18,218.7 lb (MSC-00126, section 8.13.1) [published]; its engine Apollo 11's

aps._source: The APS's load, 2,631 lb (MSC-00126, section 8.13.2), and its thrust and specific impulse in the insertion burn, 3,232 lbf and 308 s, the prediction from the flight's regulator pressure, temperatures and loads that the flight data matched (ibid., Table 8.9-I) [published]

lm_rcs._source: The LM RCS's load, 317 lb in each of its two systems (MSC-00126, section 8.13.3) [published]

sivb._source: The J-2 in AS-505's second S-IVB burn, TLI: 194,979 lbf and 429.01 s, the burn's average, and 132,934 lb of LOX with 29,021 lb of LH2 in the tanks at the second ignition (the S-IVB-505N flight evaluation report, Table 8-1 and section 8) [published; the thrust and the specific impulse held through the burn: simplified]

s_ic._source: AS-505's F-1s: 6,704.6 kN and an Isp of 264.3 s each reduced to sea level, the five engines' average at the 35 to 38 s time slice (MPR-SAT-FE-69-7, Table 5-1) [published, averaged: derived]; 8,007 kN each in vacuum at OECO, the peak 38.47 m/s2 on 832,562 kg over four engines (ibid., Tables 4-1 and 20-9) [derived], the exit area the difference over the sea level's pressure [derived]; the propellant the vehicle's mass from holddown release to OECO (ibid., Table 20-9) [derived], the vacuum Isp that burns it by the flown OECO, 161.63 s [estimated]

s_ii._source: AS-505's second flight stage at the S-II's start command, its aft interstage and launch escape system jettisoned, and 214,432 kg at its cutoff signal (MPR-SAT-FE-69-7, Table 20-9) [published], the propellant between them [derived]; five J-2s at the high mixture ratio, 5,157,611 N on 1,238.3 kg/s 61 s after the start command (ibid., section 6.3), four after the centre engine's cutoff, and 3,090,002 N on four at the low ratio after the shift (ibid.) [published], on the flow that burns the rest by the flown cutoff, 552.64 s [estimated]

s_ivb._source: AS-505's third flight stage at the S-IVB's first start command (MPR-SAT-FE-69-7, Table 20-9); the J-2 in the first burn, 204,965 lbf on 180.18 kg/s of LOX and 36.30 kg/s of LH2 (ibid., Table 7-1, whose newtons are misprinted) [published]

saturn_v._source: AS-505, Apollo 10's Saturn V, where it differs from spacecraft.json's AS-506: at holddown arm release 2,900,383 kg (MPR-SAT-FE-69-7, Table 20-9) [published]; its drag and its guidance failure's rate AS-506's [estimated]

calls.ignition: We have ignition sequence start, engines on.
calls.liftoff: Lift-off. We have lift-off, 49 minutes past the hour.

launch._comment: Apollo 10's launch from Launch Complex 39B, the only Saturn V launched from it, at 16:49:00 UTC on 18 May 1969, GET 0, on AS-505 [published]. The pad's coordinates are the postflight trajectory's (Boeing D5-15560-5, section 2), taken as geocentric [simplified]. The start phase begins on the pad at start_get_s: guidance reference release at grr_get_s (-16.97 s), the S-IC's start sequence commanded at ignition_get_s, all engines running by thrust_ok_get_s, the holddown arms' release at release_get_s and T1 at t1_get_s (Saturn V launch vehicle flight evaluation report, AS-505, MPR-SAT-FE-69-7, Tables 2-1 and 2-2) [published]. The Instrument Unit's boost program on its time bases as AS-505 flew it (ibid.) [published]: the S-IC's centre engine cutoff (135.16 s) on T1, the tilt arrest (158.7 s) on T2; T3 at the outboard engines' cutoff (161.63 s), which the propellant ends, then staging, the S-II's start, its aft interstage's separation, the launch escape tower's jettison, the iterative guidance's start, the S-II's centre engine cutoff (460.61 s) and its shift to the low mixture ratio (488.48 s, on the IU's clock, where AS-506's came on a velocity criterion); T4 at the S-II's cutoff (552.64 s), then staging and the S-IVB's ignition; T5 at the S-IVB's velocity cutoff (703.98 s), and insertion after it (713.76 s). The yaw away from the tower, the tilt's start, the attitude rate limit and the time-tilt pitch polynomial are SA-504's presettings, as Apollo 11's [estimated for AS-505, whose presettings aren't at hand; its roll and pitch began at 13.05 s, ibid.], toward the flight azimuth, 72.028 deg (ibid., section 4.1) [published]. The S-IVB loses parking_orbit_loss_kg between its first burn's end and its second start command: 133,786 kg and 132,609 kg (ibid., Table 20-9) [derived]; the simulator takes it off at insertion [simplified]. The calls are the flight's (Apollo Flight Journal, Apollo 10, day 1 part 1): the launch commentator's count and Stafford's [published; the count split between the ignition and the thrust OK: adapted]

calls: Okay. And, Mark. Mode 1 Charlie. You're looking great.
Mark. Mode IV, Apollo 10. Mode IV.
launch_aborts._comment: Apollo 10's launch abort modes, Apollo 11's (its mission.json's launch_aborts) on the same vehicles [estimated], at the times Houston marked them on Apollo 10's flight (Apollo Flight Journal, Apollo 10, day 1 part 1) [published]: Mode I Bravo at 0:41, Mode I Charlie at 1:58, S-IVB to orbit capability at 6:45 and Mode IV at 9:09. Mode III from 8 s before the S-II's cutoff, as Apollo 11's came [estimated: Houston didn't call it]. The calls are Duke's [published]

parking_orbit._comment: Apollo 10's orbit at insertion, from the AS-505 postflight trajectory (Boeing D5-15560-5, Table 4-II): inclination 32.546 deg and descending node 123.132 deg east of the launch meridian at range zero, insertion at 713.76 s at 32.700 N 52.526 W, 191.37 km [published], put in the ICRF by tools/ephemeris/parking_orbit.py from Launch Complex 39B [derived]. The report's 185.79 x 184.66 km orbit is taken as circular [simplified]. The launch start phase flies AS-505 into it

launch_refsmmat._comment: The launch pad REFSMMAT, the orientation the CMC's IMU was released at liftoff: X horizontal along the flight azimuth (72.028 deg, D5-15560-5, section 3), Z down along Launch Complex 39B's vertical, Y = Z x X, each a stable member axis in the ICRF, from tools/ephemeris/parking_orbit.py [derived]. The parking_orbit and translunar_coast start phases start aligned to it

tli._comment: TLI's conic, as the flown TLI left the stack on it: C3 -1,308,471 m2/s2 and eccentricity 0.97834, in the plane of inclination 31.698 deg and descending node 123.515 deg (D5-15560-5, Table 3-V: at TLI, 10 s after the cutoff signal) [published]; the plane in the ICRF by tools/ephemeris/parking_orbit.py [derived]. Its perigee lay 0.48 of the way through the burn's 27.0 deg arc, from the trajectory at ignition and cutoff (ibid., Table B-VII) and at TLI [derived]. The RTCC plans TLI's ignition time and energy (Rtcc.plan_tli()) for the free return the flown TLI left the stack on, past the Moon 907.7 nmi up at 76:10:18.4 (MSC-00126, Table 6-III) [published]. The midcourse corrections then aim at pericynthion_alt_km, at pericynthion_get, where Apollo 10's only one left it (60.9 nmi at 76:00:15.2, ibid.) [published], and by nodal targeting (node_targeting): the pericynthion in the plane of the lunar orbit over the landing site at the landing time, where LOI-1 turns the orbit into it, as the flight's did: the G mission's ground track, for the LM to approach the site as the first landing would (ibid., section 6.4; the planned LOI-1 turned the orbit 6.1 deg into a plane 1.2 deg to the lunar equator, MSC Internal Note 69-FM-96, section 5.7) [published]. earliest_get_s: 2:05:00, ahead of the S-IVB's restart preparation at 2:07:09 (ibid., Table 6-II)

loi._comment: LOI-1's targets: the final PAD's 169.2 by 59.5 nmi at its TIG, 75:55:53.31 (Apollo Flight Journal, 73:31:24; flown 170.0 by 60.2 nmi, MSC-00126, section 6.5) [published], above the Moon's mean radius [simplified]. The RTCC solves the burn at that TIG (Rtcc.plan_loi()), the orbit's plane over the landing site

doi._comment: Descent orbit insertion: the LM's pericynthion at 50,000 ft above the landing site's radius, 15 deg uprange of the site, where the landing's powered descent would begin (the spacecraft operational trajectory for Apollo 10, MSC Internal Note 69-FM-96, section 5.11.2) [published], on the pass that would land at the landing time

landing._comment: No landing: Apollo 10's LM flew its descent orbit down to 8 nmi, over Apollo Landing Site 2, the first landing's planned site, 0 deg 44 min N, 23 deg 39 min E (the final flight plan, Table 1-3) [published]. The site's height is the terrain's there (data/terrain/). Its landing time is the one a descent would have had: powered descent would have begun at 100:43:45.50, the PDI abort PAD's TIG (Apollo Flight Journal, 98:32:48) [published], the descent's 730 s before it lands (spacecraft.json descent_guidance) [derived]. The DOI PAD aims the LM's low point there, and the midcourse correction and LOI put the lunar orbit's plane over the site then

rendezvous._comment: The coelliptic sequence after the insertion: CSI at the LM's first apolune; TPI 2 h 25 min 43 s after the insertion's cutoff, the CSI PAD's N37 (105:21:01, Apollo Flight Journal, 103:14:07; the insertion cut off at 102:55:17.6, MSC-00126, Table 6-II), flown at 105:22:55.6; the midcourse corrections 15 and 30 min after TPI (105:37:56 and 105:52:56, ibid., section 4) [published]. The CSM state vector the ground uplinks with the CSI PAD is off by MSFN's tracking error, Apollo 11's [estimated]

lunar_orbit._comment: Apollo 10's lunar orbit after LOI-2, above the landing site's radius: 61.0 by 59.2 nmi, LOI-2 cutting off at 80:25:22.0 at 0.57 N 152.70 E, 59.3 nmi up and 0.01 deg climbing, just past the perilune (MSC-00126, Tables 6-II and 6-IV) [published; the perilune there: derived]. The lunar_orbit start phase starts there, placed along the orbit for the flown undocking and DOI; LOI-2's PAD targets 60.1 by 60.1 nmi (Apollo Flight Journal, 78:40:38) [published]. The SPS gave 972 m/s to here: the evasive maneuver, MCC-1, LOI-1 and LOI-2 (18.8, 49.2, 2,982.4 and 139.0 ft/s, MSC-00126, Tables 6-III and 6-IV) [published]

tei._comment: TEI onto Apollo 10's return: 3,630.2 ft/s at 137:36:28.9 for 164.8 s, the SPS's velocity gained (MSC-00126, Table 7.6-V; Table 6-V's 3,680.3 ft/s is a misprint) [published]; the TEI-31 PAD's TIG, 137:36:28.21, and N81 +3,625.2, +40.0, +188.0 ft/s, from which the RTCC starts its solve (Apollo Flight Journal, 135:57:30) [published]; entry interface came at 191:48:54.5, 23.60 S 174.39 E, 36,314 ft/s, 6.54 deg down, heading 71.89 deg east of north (MSC-00126, Table 6-II) [published]. That state, put in the simulator, is on a return inclined 29.32 deg to the equator with its vacuum perigee 34.0 km up (Rtcc.vacuum_perigee()) [derived]. The RTCC solves the burn at the flown TEI's time for that inclination, that entry interface and that corridor (Rtcc.plan_tei())

entry._comment: Apollo 10's target, N61 in the entry PAD at 187:43:13, unchanged in its last update at 190:49:05 (Apollo Flight Journal): 15.07 deg S, 164.67 deg W, 1,204 nmi from entry interface [published]. The ground uplinks it with the entry PAD (the timeline's entry_pad), and the entry start phase starts with it loaded

lgc._comment: Snoopy's IMU (slice 11a): its gyros' drift, +5.1, -1.5 and -1.9 mERU, from the torquing of its P52 at 101:30, -0.169, +0.050 and +0.066 deg, over the 2.2 h since its P52 at 99:20 (the table's drift column: +5.1, -1.5 and +1.9); the first P52 after undocking, on stars 33 (Antares) and 25 (Acrux), its star angle difference 0.09 deg and its N93 -0.668, -0.195 and -0.055 deg (Apollo 10 Mission Report, MSC-00126, Table 8.6-II) [published]. The drift's sign is the torquing's reverse on each axis, the platform's own turn over the time between: the tables' mERU columns give Z's the other way, where Apollo 11's Table 9.6-II gives all three so [derived]

dispersions._comment: The seed the flight's dispersions are drawn from: the CSM's unmodelled forces (spacecraft.json "unmodelled"), once for the flight, and MSFN's tracking error ("msfn"), for each uplink

msfn._comment: The Manned Space Flight Network's tracking error in the CSM state vector the RTCC plans the CSM's PADs from and uplinks with them (P27): standard deviations in LVLH (X along track, Y right, Z down), by the body the CSM's orbit is about, Apollo 11's [estimated]

timeline._comment: Mission Control from TLI to the entry. Each entry happens once: at its GET ('get'), or 's' seconds 'after' a mission event or a planned time, or 'before' a planned time (the sequencer's plan), if its condition ('when', a flight phase or one of the sequencer's) holds then; CAPCOM makes the call ('say') and the ground uplinks the PAD ('pad'): the RTCC's solution, a midcourse correction's at its TIG ('tig'), TEI's at the opportunity nearest 'near', or a maneuver the flight plan fixed ('n81_ft_s', LVLH): the CSM's at 'tig', the LM's on its 'engine' 'tig_s' seconds after a planned time ('tig_after'), the DPS on the PAD's 'throttle' schedule. The times, calls and PADs are Apollo 10's [published: the Apollo Flight Journal: GO for TLI 2:30:32; the evasive maneuver PAD 3:29:01; the MCC-1 PAD 25:37:52; the final LOI-1 PAD 73:31:24; GO for LOI 74:46:49; the LOI-2 PAD 78:40:38; the CSM separation PAD 97:13:22; GO for undocking 97:36:18; the DOI PAD 98:28:05, 16 min 8 s after undocking at 98:11:57 (MSC-00126); GO for DOI 99:36:47, 554 s before DOI; the phasing PAD with DOI's, TIG 100:58:25.20, 879.7 s after the PDI abort PAD's 100:43:45.50, and no update to it at 100:29:49; GO for phasing 100:49:22, 543 s before it; the insertion PAD 101:09:31, TIG 102:55:01.40, 7,875.9 s after the PDI abort PAD's; the LM's state vector 102:23:00; GO for staging 102:40:15; the CSI update 103:13:54, 18 min 36 s after the insertion's cutoff at 102:55:17.6 (MSC-00126); 'looking good for Sep' 108:18:28, 1 h 56 min 26 s after docking at 106:22:02 (MSC-00126); the TEI-31 PAD's last update 135:57:30; GO for TEI 136:57:49; the MCC-6 PAD 165:38:59, TIG 176:49:57.28, and the MCC-7 PAD 187:39:35, TIG 188:49:56.75, MCC-6 not flown; the entry PAD's last update 190:49:05; GO for pyro arm 191:31:23], except the entries marked estimated. The CSM's separation maneuver is the mission report's, 2.5 ft/s radially down at 98:47:16 (MSC-00126, section 4) [published]

entries.say: Roger, 10. You're Go for TLI. S-IVB is looking as planned.

entries._estimated: the PAD's time, an hour before MCC-4's, 5 h before LOI (MSC-00126, section 6.4): the ground deleted MCC-4 at 70:17:47, its 2.8 ft/s not needed with the perilune 60.7 nmi up; the RTCC here flies it when the tracking has the approach off

entries.say: That's affirmative, 10. And we've polled the room and you are Go for LOI. Over.
Okay. {csm} and Snoop, 3 minutes going over the hill. You're Go for undocking, and we'll see you around the other side.
{csm}, Houston. Forty-five seconds to LOS. You're still Go for DOI.

entries.name: PHASING
entries._throttle: 26 s at 10 %, then full thrust (MSC Internal Note 69-FM-96, section 5.11.3; flown 40.0 s, MSC-00126, Table 6-IV)

entries.say: OK. Roger. Pass it on: we got 9 minutes till burn; get in the attitude; and they're Go for phasing. Over.
Roger. We'd like you to go to P00 and Accept. We have a state vector for you.
Snoop, Houston. We have you Go for staging. Over.
Hello, Snoop. Houston. We have a CSI update for you. Over.
Okay. We're looking good for Sep here, now, Tom.
Apollo 10, this is Houston. We show about 10 minutes until LOS, and at this time everything looks Go for TEI.
That's affirmative, 10. You are Go for Pyro Arm.

start_notes.parking_orbit: In the parking orbit, TLI ahead
start_notes.lunar_descent: Snoopy on its descent orbit, 20 min before the low pass
